name: @playform/ets-plugin-dsh-workspace-authority
description: The workspace-authority service: a DeepSeek plugin that IS the authority step of the workspace family's invisible flow - the licenses. The service keeps the THREE SEPARATE AUTHORITY RECORDS (v4.1 section 3.9, correcting the corpus's own conflation): the CAPABILITY (what the actor may do - the holder, the resource, the permitted operations, the expiration, the delegation rule, the revocation), the LEASE (for how long - the holder, the resource, the acquisition, the expiry), and the RESIDENCY (what stays in the store - the resource, the kind, the weight). Three records, three owners; the capability, the lease and the residency are never one object. THE EVICTION DISPOSITIONS are keep, defer, evict, discard, promote - decided by the policy table (a small table of rules per resource kind, with defaults, TTLs and the revocation timing); THE LICENSE DECIDES, THE WEIGHT ONLY RANKS (the license/weight conflation is a logged pitfall: priority, retention and permission are never interchangeable - the residency record carries the weight in its own field and the policy never reads it except to order candidates). The service exposes ctx.workspaceAuthority: grant/revoke (capabilities), authorize (the holder, the resource, the operation - an expired, revoked or unpermitted capability denies with a byte-stable ledger line), acquire/release (leases with lazy expiry sweep), residence, evict (the disposition pass), statistics. The plugin ships DISABLED - the idle-forever posture: the service registers and reads honestly, but grants and leases nothing until enabled; a cold mount logs `disabled (enabled=false)`. Plan: Documentation/Plans/Workspace-Family/AUTHORITY.md + Documentation/Plans/WORKSPACE-FAMILY-V4-1.md section 3.9.
